note: The fuzzer interprets attacker bytes as 32-bit code points and derives the logical string length from the raw input size.
The input buffer is passed directly to FriBidi as the source text.
FriBidi computes bidi classes from the attacker-controlled text, which determines later run segmentation.
The bidi classes are encoded into a linked run list with prev/next and isolate links.
The algorithm compacts adjacent runs before weak-type resolution, so attacker-chosen adjacency can trigger node merges.

code: if (RL_TYPE (list->prev) == RL_TYPE (list) && RL_LEVEL (list->prev) == RL_LEVEL (list) ... ) list = merge_with_prev (list);
note: When two neighboring runs match in type and level, the current node is merged into the previous one.
The merge updates the successor's isolate back-pointer using the soon-to-be-freed node, creating a stale-pointer write primitive.
The merged run node is freed immediately after the pointer rewiring, so any later use of that node becomes a use-after-free.
This write is the memory-safety sink: the code dereferences and stores through a node whose lifetime is no longer valid under the compaction path exercised by the crafted input.
